record.paper_title: Results and Open Questions on the Boundary Control of Moving Sets
record.original_question: Let V⊂R^2 be an open connected domain with bounded perimeter, and consider the constrained eradication problem (CEP) for moving contaminated sets Ω(t)⊆V under the boundary-effort constraint described in Section 6. Determine the strategy t→Ω(t) that eradicates the contamination in minimum time for a general such domain V. In particular, characterize the optimal strategy when V is a polygon and when V is a convex domain with smooth boundary.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, there are many domains V ⊂ R2 for which the conditions in Theorem 7.2 are not satisfied by any map t 7→ Ω(t) ⊆ V . For example, think of a triangle. Another example is shown in Fig. 20, left. This leads to our third main open problem:

Problem 3. Given an open connected domain V ⊂ R2 with bounded perimeter, describe the optimal strategy t 7→ Ω(t) ⊆ V for (CEP), achieving the eradication in minimum time. In particular, it would be of interest to study the cases where (i) V is a polygon, or (ii) V is a convex set with smooth boundary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be an open connected domain with bounded perimeter, and fix a constant $M > 0$ representing the total boundary-effort budget per unit time. A contaminated set is a measurable subset $\Omega(t) \subseteq V$ evolving in time $t \ge 0$. In the absence of control, the boundary of $\Omega(t)$ that lies in the interior of $V$ propagates outward with unit normal speed, while the part of the boundary lying on $\partial V$ is fixed (geographical barrier). A control strategy is an inward normal velocity $\beta(t,x) \ge 0$ assigned along the free part of $\partial \Omega(t)$ (i.e., $\partial \Omega(t) \cap V$), so that the boundary moves with normal velocity $1 - \beta(t,x)$. The strategy is admissible if at almost every time $t$
$$\int_{\partial \Omega(t) \cap V} \beta(t,x)\, d\mathcal{H}^1(x) \le M.$$
Given an initial contaminated set $\Omega(0) = \Omega_0 \subseteq V$, the constrained eradication problem (CEP) asks for an admissible strategy $t \mapsto \Omega(t)$ such that $\Omega(T) = \emptyset$ for some finite $T$, minimizing the eradication time $T$.

Problem: For a general open connected domain $V \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with bounded perimeter, describe the optimal strategy $t \mapsto \Omega(t) \subseteq V$ achieving eradication in minimum time. In particular, characterize the minimum-time optimal strategy in the following two cases:
(i) $V$ is a polygon;
(ii) $V$ is a convex domain with smooth boundary.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem in a February 2025 survey on boundary control of moving sets. Companion work from the same period addresses related existence and optimality results, but no general characterization of the minimum-time optimal strategy for arbitrary $V$ (or for the polygonal/convex-smooth subcases) appears to be available. No subsequent resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Results and open questions on the boundary control of moving sets
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing this as a third main open problem regarding minimum-time eradication strategies on general planar domains, polygons, and smooth convex sets.

status_evidence.title: Optimally Controlled Moving Sets with Geographical Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Companion paper providing existence, sufficient/necessary optimality conditions, and explicit optima in special cases, but not a full characterization for general $V$.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results without resolving the general problem.
